title: Quantitative low-degree affine Koszul orthogonality and open localization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A$. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme], $W=\bigcup_{k=1}^rD(f_k)$ with $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$, and let $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be the open immersion. Use the Zariski structure sheaf and its unbounded derived category with quasi-coherent cohomology subcategory [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $C_f\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be obtained by sheafifying the Koszul complex $K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] termwise and placing $K_q$ in cochain degree $-q$. For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and integer $a$, if
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_Y)}(C_f[-n],E)=0\quad\text{for every integer }n\leq a,$$
then the canonical restriction-adjunction unit induces an isomorphism in the derived category
$$\tau_{\leq a-1}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\leq a-1}Rj_*(j^*E).$$
Here $Rj_*$ is the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $\tau_{\leq a}$ is standard cohomological truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. This includes $r=0$, when $W=\varnothing$ and $C_f=\mathcal O_Y[0]$.

proof.text: Each $D(f_k)$ is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{f_k})$ by the localization/basic-open node, and that spectrum is quasi-compact by the basic-opens/unit-ideal node. An open cover of $W$ therefore has a finite subcover on each of its finitely many $D(f_k)$, and their union is finite. This also handles $r=0$. Put $B=Rj_*(j^*E)$. By ringed-space derived adjunction, $Rj_*$ is right adjoint to $Lj^*$, which for this open immersion is exact restriction: the inverse image of the structure sheaf is the structure sheaf on the open. Let $u:E\to B$ be the canonical unit. Complete $u$ to a distinguished triangle $E\xrightarrow{u}B\to N\to E[1]$. The derived open-unit-cone node applies because $W$ is quasi-compact and $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. It gives $N\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $j^*N=0$. Here $N$ is the cone, not the fibre.

proof.text: The Koszul restriction-zero node gives $j^*(C_f[m])=0$ for every integer $m$. Derived adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[m],B)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*C_f[m],j^*E)=0$. Fix $n\leq a-1$. Shift invariance gives $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[-n],E[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[-(n+1)],E)=0$, since $n+1\leq a$. For any $v:C_f[-n]\to N$, its composite into $E[1]$ is zero. Hom-into-triangle exactness on the rotated triangle $B\to N\to E[1]\to B[1]$ factors $v$ through $B$. The latter Hom group is zero, so $v=0$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(C_f[-n],N)=0$ for every $n\leq a-1$. This is the endpoint correction: with $N$ the cone, the Hom group into $E$ is in degree $n+1$, not $n$.

proof.text: For every positive exponent tuple $\mathbf e=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$, let $C_{\mathbf e}$ be the sheafified cochain Koszul object for $(f_i^{e_i})$. Prove $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\mathbf e}[-n],N)=0$ for all $n\leq a-1$ by strong induction on $\sum_i(e_i-1)$. At sum zero all exponents are one, so Step 2 applies. Otherwise choose $i$ with $e_i>1$ and keep the other coordinates fixed. The coordinate multiplication triangle, with scalars $f_i^{e_i-1}$ and $f_i$, has outer objects with coordinate exponents $e_i-1$ and $1$, and middle object $C_{\mathbf e}$. Both outer tuples have smaller induction measure. Shift this triangle by $-n$. For any map from its middle object to $N$, precomposition from the first object is zero by induction; Hom-out-of-triangle exactness factors it through the third object, whose Hom to $N$ is also zero by induction. This proves the claim at the same $n$. For $r=0$ the induction measure is zero and there is no induction step.

proof.text: Fix $n\leq a-1$ and $\varphi:\mathcal O_Y[-n]\to N$. Apply supported-augmentation vanishing to $N$ and this shift: its hypotheses hold by Step 1. It supplies an index $e\in\mathbf N$ with $\varphi\circ u_e[-n]=0$. Its convention is that index $e$ means exponent $e+1$. The represent-cohomology node supplies the triangle $I_e\xrightarrow{u_e}\mathcal O_Y\to K_e\to I_e[1]$, where $K_e=C_{(e+1,\ldots,e+1)}$. Apply Hom-out-of-triangle exactness to its shift by $-n$: $\varphi$ factors through $K_e[-n]$. Step 3 makes this factor zero, so $\varphi=0$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y[-n],N)=0$ for all $n\leq a-1$.

proof.text: Apply the structure-sheaf Hom/hypercohomology bijection to $N[n]$. Shifting the source identifies its Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y[-n],N)$, zero by Step 4, so $H^0(R\Gamma(Y,N[n]))=0$. The affine derived equivalence is triangulated, hence its quasi-inverse $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ commutes with shifts; thus this is $H^n(R\Gamma(Y,N))=0$. Write $F$ for the equivalence from $D(A)$ to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ induced by termwise associated sheaf. Since $N$ is quasi-coherent, its counit gives $F(R\Gamma(Y,N))\simeq N$. The affine tilde/homology comparison applies to this very $F$ and gives $H^n(N)\simeq\widetilde{H^n(R\Gamma(Y,N))}=0$ for every $n\leq a-1$. In particular this uses the cohomology comparison, not merely conservativity of the affine equivalence.

proof.text: For $n\leq a-1$, the cohomological-functor clause (5) of the heart/triangle theorem applied to $E\xrightarrow{u}B\to N\to E[1]$ gives the exact segment $H^{n-1}(N)\to H^n(E)\xrightarrow{H^n(u)}H^n(B)\to H^n(N)$. Both outside objects vanish by Step 5, since $n-1\leq a-1$ as well. Therefore $H^n(u)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\leq a-1$. Standard truncation retains these cohomology objects and kills those in degrees greater than $a-1$, so $\tau_{\leq a-1}(u)$ induces isomorphisms on every cohomology object. Notice that this argument does not assert an isomorphism in degree $a$.

proof.text: A morphism of derived objects that induces isomorphisms on every cohomology object is invertible: use the cited calculus of quasi-isomorphisms and right-fraction representation in the homotopy category to represent it by a roof $P\xleftarrow{s}Q\xrightarrow{t}R$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. Since $H^n(s)$ and the cohomology maps of the roof are invertible, $H^n(t)$ is invertible for every $n$ as well. Thus both arrows of the roof are inverted in the localization defining the derived category. Apply this to $\tau_{\leq a-1}(u)$ from Step 6. This proves the claimed isomorphism for the canonical unit itself.
